ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: The horizontal axis in the figure successively marks the spring equinox, summer solstice, autumn equinox, winter solstice, and spring equinox; the right vertical axis is day length, marked with 0, 6, 12, 18, and 24 hours. Curve 5 passes through 12 hours near the spring equinox and autumn equinox, reaches about 18 hours 30 minutes near the summer solstice, and falls to about 5 hours 30 minutes near the winter solstice. In the figure, 1, 2, 3, and 4 are broken lines of seasonal variation of noon solar altitude, among which the noon solar altitude of place 4 is lower near the summer solstice and higher near the winter solstice, showing that it is located in the Southern Hemisphere; while the place represented by curve 5 has the same latitude degree as place 4 but is in the opposite Northern/Southern Hemisphere. Then reason: On the same date, the day lengths of places at the same latitude in the Northern and Southern Hemispheres are complements of 24 hours. The summer solstice day length at the place of curve 5 is about 18 hours 30 minutes, so the summer solstice day length of place 4 in the opposite hemisphere is about 24 hours - 18 hours 30 minutes = 5 hours 30 minutes, so the summer solstice night length at place 4 is 24 hours - 5 hours 30 minutes = 18 hours 30 minutes. At the winter solstice, place 4 is located in the Southern Hemisphere, and the day length in the Southern Hemisphere at the same latitude equals the summer solstice day length at the corresponding latitude in the Northern Hemisphere, namely about 18 hours 30 minutes. Therefore, the summer solstice night length and winter solstice day length at place 4 are both 18 hours 30 minutes.

First describe the image: The horizontal axis in the figure successively marks the spring equinox, summer solstice, autumn equinox, winter solstice, and spring equinox; the right vertical axis is day length, marked with 0, 6, 12, 18, and 24 hours. Curve 5 passes through 12 hours near the spring equinox and autumn equinox, reaches about 18 hours 30 minutes near the summer solstice, and falls to about 5 hours 30 minutes near the winter solstice. In the figure, 1, 2, 3, and 4 are broken lines of seasonal variation of noon solar altitude, among which the noon solar altitude of place 4 is lower near the summer solstice and higher near the winter solstice, showing that it is located in the Southern Hemisphere; while the place represented by curve 5 has the same latitude degree as place 4 but is in the opposite Northern/Southern Hemisphere.
Then reason: On the same date, the day lengths of places at the same latitude in the Northern and Southern Hemispheres are complements of 24 hours.
